reasons.D: Closest match: formal Latinate diction ('possessed', 'occasion so much inconvenience', 'resided'), dry mock-ceremonious irony, long hedged sentences with embedded asides, and quoted exchanges folded into the narration.
reasons.A: Uses the editorial 'we' and a long piled-up catalogue sentence like the passage, with dashes and gentle irony, but its warm closing reflection and short emphatic sentences are softer and more modern than the author's.
reasons.C: Has the period register and some polysyndeton, but first-person 'I', chatty fragments ('A handsome thought.', 'Well,') and a clipped, staccato rhythm move away from the author's long, fussy, qualified sentences.
reasons.B: Plain modern prose with contemporary phrasing ('actually works', 'a very human one'), even sentence rhythm and an earnest explanatory tone; it lacks the author's archaic formality and ironic distance.
